lastCompletedAction: OF-016 correction loop 2 of 2 (FINAL). Review 2 confirmed all eight round-1 findings genuinely closed -- it reproduced each on a pre-fix database and could not get around any fix, including a bespoke role, COPY, TRUNCATE CASCADE, session_replication_role='replica' and ALTER TABLE DISABLE TRIGGER against the evidence boundary -- and found four more. J-02 (P1) is the material one and it is the package re-creating its own blocker one layer up: the detector writes ONE review per match, so a payment resembling TWO earlier ones raises two open reviews; confirming one moved the event to `duplicate`, which is terminal, and the sibling was then resolvable in NEITHER direction by anyone -- the state guard refused both, 0087's triggers refused service_role, and no api role holds DML. The queue showed it forever and the button told the reviewer to reload. Untested because every earlier test seeded exactly one review per event. Migration 0089 closes the event's other open reviews in the same transaction as `superseded_by_decision`, a third outcome that is explicitly NOT a human verdict on that pair, names the deciding review and audits itself as such. Dismissal deliberately leaves siblings open -- releasing one pair says nothing about another, and closing them would be the silent merge this work exists to prevent. J-01: my 'the pipeline repeats the check as defence in depth' was FALSE -- the guard took a parameter no call site passed and could not, because findDuplicates runs before createDraft; the real second layer now lives in openDuplicateReview where the id exists. J-03: clearing the dead-letter stamp while preserving spent attempts was a HALF revival -- one ordinary provider error killed the released payment again, with no second release available; the budget is restored and the prior count goes into the audit. J-04: I left the false '24 tests' claim standing beside its own correction, which is the G-05 mistake this register already names. Also corrected: the three operator surfaces counted review ROWS, so one paused payment rendered as '2 payments are paused'; they now count distinct payments, because that is what their labels say.

openFindings: OF-016: RESOLVED by migration 0087 (pending independent review). The paused payment now has an authorized, audited, idempotent resolution path and a screen; historic 0083 rows work as they stand.

OF-018: RESOLVED by migration 0090 and locally accepted at 5109bc0. The two inbound-review RPCs now authorize solely by their exact service_role EXECUTE grants; direct service sessions remain valid without or despite claim text, while anon/authenticated remain denied.

OF-017 (P1, INHERENT -- not closed by FOUND-006): under the PostgREST shared-login model every API session authenticates as `authenticator`, which Supabase grants membership of both `authenticated` and `service_role`. SET ROLE is authorised against session_user, so a caller with arbitrary SQL as `authenticated` can `set role service_role` and reach every service-only entrypoint. No in-database control can close this while the login role holds both memberships; it requires a separate connection identity for service work, which is an owner infrastructure decision.

OF-014 residual (P1): a caller with arbitrary SQL as the `authenticated` DB role can forge request.jwt.claims — reading one quotation status per id, and more broadly forging `sub` and so auth.uid(). The unauthenticated half is closed. Belongs to FOUND-006.
